scope: Windows 11 x64 development host. Isolated desktop fixtures and temporary folders. Loopback model only.
before: On the prior test executable, a real CloseMainWindow request destroyed the main webview with a dirty, conflicted folder transcript and a streaming reply in a pinned project. Native test failed at the assertion that the window should remain open.

exitCases: Cancellation during a failing manual write does not open a stale recovery dialog.
Concurrent closes wait for one manual write and its late reply. Temporary conversations stay in memory.
An executing local file operation keeps the window open and other requests running.
An automatic plan arriving during exit remains available for manual review on return.

observations: Two Windows close requests produced a single recovery dialog. Keep allowed a second streamed fragment from the original provider request to reach pinned project B.
A third close and Save as new left the external revision and the local copy in A. The pinned B archive read after native process exit contained the marked partial reply with omitHistory set.
The hidden tray smoke window was restored by the same menu exit action and delivered a preventable native CloseRequested event.

The tray test exited successfully. Chromium logged a window-class unregister warning (1412) at teardown. A subsequent process check found no fixture host or WebView2 process matching either test profile.

verification.build: 532 files verified after source ZIP extraction. Offline MSVC release from that extraction using a shared target cache. Every package hash, exact release executable, Cargo.lock and runtime manifest pin were checked.

limits: Native coverage used an OS close request and the tray menu callback. It did not synthesize a physical Alt+F4 keystroke or click Explorer notification-area pixels.
Unsent drafts, deliberately temporary chats and abrupt system or process termination are outside normal close protection.
The frozen M5 RC6 clean Windows 10/11 and authenticated provider acceptance gates remain open.
